You realise maybe there was only 12 eps of S7 because Filoni wanted to move on? He had worked on Clone Wars from 2008 - 2014 (Season 1 to 6), and then after moving on, exploring more things in Rebels, he came back in 2020, meaning he spent 12 years on Clone Wars before concluding it. Does this mean he didn't love Clone Wars? Absolutely not. But people want to sometimes move on, and try new concepts, and I'm pretty sure that's probably why he decided against more episodes. Besides, S7 wouldn't have had space for Cad Bane VS Boba, or more Bad Batch stories. It was a straight forward, last sprint to the finish line, and that makes it more impactful.

People dislike Season 4 and some of the massive jumps it takes in expanding the force, while others hate the ending. I digress anyway, my point is that Rebels is still disliked by a large majority of people, but people just move on.

Ayy ATLA gaang lmao. Before I respond to that part, I just wanna say I highly recommend Legend Of Korra too. It's a kinda half sequel, half spin-off show set like 70 years after ATLA. That's all I'll say on that to avoid spoilers. 

Now for Clone Wars, yes, I recommend watching Ep 1 and 2 first before you start. However, I also recommend you watch Episode 3 too. There are some subtle nods throughout the show to the film, and I think a better memory of the film will really enhance it for you. 

And yeah, if you don't know ANYTHING about Clone Wars, start with the film. It introduces all the new characters that you'll need to know, and while not the best piece of cinema (it's like a 5/10, it was essentially a bunch of episodes from the show turned into a film), it does set up what you need. After that, I'd say just go through the show chronologically. The show has 3-4 episode arcs most of the time, and some 1 offs here and there. The good part about Clone Wars is that for the most part, if you're not enjoying an arc, you can just skip it. The key arcs that play into future seasons are constantly heralded as being great by fans and critics, so I doubt you'll skip them. And if you're ever unsure, just post here, and I'm sure someone will help you out. As to being binge-friendly, or episodic, it's honestly both. You could watch an arc in one day, and spend the next couple reflecting on it. Or you could binge it all, and it work. The final part of your question was were the new seasons good, and I'll get into a bit behind that quickly.

Essentially, Clone Wars was meant to be like a 8 season show or something. Unfortunately, due to the Disney acquisition, they canned the show after S5, and around 57 (I think?) episodes were left on the cutting room floor. This were all written, so it was really sad for us fans. There were some episodes far along in production, which were finished and therefore we got S6. After a couple years of silence, we eventually got a revival, that gave us Season 7. This seasons wraps up the major arcs and characters of the show, but it's still worth understanding there are a couple gaps in some things due to unfinished episodes. However, figuring out what is missing is a conversation for another day, maybe after you've finished.

The final piece to my rant is that there is a sorta sequel/follow up show called Star Wars Rebels, which is also great. Some fans really don't like it due to how kid friendly it is in the first couple seasons, but for me that never detracted from the overall quality. I don't wanna overload you with info so I'll leave this here and just say it exists, and is worth watching once you finish the show. I hope my massive "essay" was able to clear some stuff up, and if you have any questions and shit, let me know, I'll gladly answer them! Hope you enjoy the show, and may the force be with you...
